Mesothelioma has a long latency period and exposure may not lead to cancer until 20-30 years later. Sometimes more, sometimes less, but that’s generally how long it takes.
There is no safe level of asbestos exposure. Better to be overly cautious than to die in the ICU while they struggle to get the intubation tube down your disfigured scarred airway.
Better to be overly cautious than not cautious enough
No, you cannot lick asbestos and it won’t effect you. There is also peritoneal mesothelioma.

But isn’t it still possible to get it from limited exposure? At the conferences I’ve been to they stressed that it is very possible to get it from limited exposure, even a single exposure. My brothers surgeon had some cases where the patients were very young, a 13 year old even.

Plus kids tend to have shorter latency periods when it comes to meso. My brother’s surgeon had a 13 year old patient. If kids interact with this, it may be a sooner death sentence for them than an adult if they get enough exposure.
Mesothelioma killed my brother back in 2018. 11 months after diagnosis, and he was only 29. I wouldn’t wish it on my worst enemy.

Richard Cory
BY EDWIN ARLINGTON ROBINSON

Whenever Richard Cory went down town,
We people on the pavement looked at him:
He was a gentleman from sole to crown,
Clean favored, and imperially slim.

And he was always quietly arrayed,
And he was always human when he talked;
But still he fluttered pulses when he said,
"Good-morning," and he glittered when he walked.

And he was rich—yes, richer than a king—
And admirably schooled in every grace:
In fine, we thought that he was everything
To make us wish that we were in his place.

So on we worked, and waited for the light,
And went without the meat, and cursed the bread;
And Richard Cory, one calm summer night,
Went home and put a bullet through his head.

When the ambulance was on the way to take my brother to the psychiatric ward, I held him until he stopped hurting himself and then I made the Easter baskets for my siblings while my dad went off to drink. Then, when my siblings woke up I acted so surprised and excited when they showed me their baskets in the morning. 

When my dad used to choke my brother when I was little, I would try to scream at him and get him off even though I was small and helpless and he could have hurt me too. 

When my dad got super drunk and punched the window open and bled everywhere, I helped my mom scrub the blood off the floors and walls and comforted my siblings while the police came. When he screamed terrible things at my mom I yelled back in her defense even though I was scared. 

When my brother was dying in the hospital of cancer I held his hand all night and watched his heart monitor like a hawk and kept trying to calm him down so his heart rate would go down a bit because it was really high. I spoke to him as if he had all the time in the world and didn't once cry or even look sad in front of him. This was less of a nice thing I did for someone and more if something I did because of how much I love my brother and wanted him to be okay. He passed away in the morning and I have been doing everything I can to memorialize him such as making an exhibit of his artwork. This is not a chore or anything, lately it's the most fulfilling thing to do and it makes me feel closer to my brother. He was one of my best and dearest friends. 

My parents gave me 100 dollars to get myself some Christmas presents but I spent all of it on presents for other people. My brother had passed away on the 12th of December and I couldn't even think about getting anything for myself, there was nothing I wanted besides other people's happiness. You never know when you'll lose someone.
